Name: Don't Panic
Notes: Track 1 of Parachutes. 11th song to be written by the band, originally called Panic. This is also one of the only songs that Jonny sings on. This version was re-produced by Ken Nelson. The song was recorded live, with Jonny overdubbing guitar parts. Recorded in Rockfield Studios in Wales, and Parr Street Studio in Liverpool. Later released as the fourth and final single from Parachutes.

Name: Shiver
Notes: Track 2 of Parachutes and the lead single of the album. Supposedly written 2 years before release. The song was heavily speculated to be written about Natalie Imbruglia, though Chris has denied this. It is also very inspired by the music of Jeff Buckley, which Chris was listening to while writing the song. It was produced by Ken Nelson and recorded in Rockfield Studios in Wales.

Name: Spies
Notes: Track 3 of Parachutes, rewritten from the Blue Room Era. Produced by Ken Nelson and mostly recorded in Rockfield Studios across 3 days, and was apparently one of the hardest to record on the whole album.

Name: Sparks
Notes: Track 4 of Parachutes. Produced by Ken Nelson and recorded at the time as We Never Change as 'basically a live take'. Recently the song has had a chart resurgence due to blowing up on TikTok. Later re-released on the Acoustic EP, which is also known as the Sparks EP.

Name: Yellow
Notes: Track 5 of Parachutes and its second single. The song was written at Rockfield Studios during a break from recording Shiver. It originally started out by Chris playing on acoustic guitar, where he wrote the verse. Will and Jonny didn't care for the song when they were presented it, they were busy playing FIFA. While recording in England, the band had Yellow mixed in New York. Unhappy with the results, they flew over to personally ensure the track achieved the sound they envisioned. It was produced by Ken Nelson and became one of the bands biggest hits.

Name: Trouble
Notes: Track 6 of Parachutes and the album's third single. The song has 2 different music videos, one being dubbed the 'UK Version'. It was originally written as an apology for Chris kicking Will out of the band, and it stemmed from a demo called Spiderwebs. The song is apparently inspired by Supergrass. Produced by Ken Nelson and took 4 takes to record.

Name: Parachutes
Notes: Track 7 and the title track of Parachutes. Chris tried an extended, instrumental version played on piano but eventually decided on the guitar arrangement. Produced by Ken Nelson and took multiple takes to finish.

Notes: Track 8 of Parachutes. Re-released from The Blue Room EP. A newer version for Parachutes was recorded, but for some reason not picked to be on the album. Produced by Chris Allison.

Name: Politik
Notes: Track 1 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. The song was written on 9/11 after the events that day, and recorded 2 days later. Chris stated that the band wanted to write a song where they could hit their instruments as hard as they could. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head

Notes: Track 2 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head and the album's lead single. The song was originally recorded during the Parachutes era and throughout the next 2 years would spawn over 100 different versions. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: God Put a Smile upon Your Face
Notes: Track 3 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head and the album's fourth and final single. The song was originally called Your Guess Is As Good As Mine, and was supposedly hard to record, something felt 'missing'. It was produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: The Scientist
Notes: Track 4 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head and its second single. The song was written after Chris listened to George Harrison's All Things Must Pass. He had found an old out of tune piano in Liverpool and started to play the song, accidentally writing The Scientist. Both the original piano and vocal takes were recorded here. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: Clocks
Notes: Track 5 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head and its third single. It was the 11th song to be written for AROBTTH and is inspired by Muse. Will thought the song was terrible and that it lacked a chorus, so a demo was recorded to be worked on for album 3. However, after Phil Harvery had heard it he convinced the band to re-record the song and put it on the album. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: Daylight
Notes: Track 6 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. Written in Liverpool at the same time as The Scientist and supposedly recorded 'very fact'. The song features Jonny giving backing vocals throughout most of it. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: Green Eyes
Notes: Track 7 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. Written for a friend of Chris' who he had met in Mexico. It has been described as a 'silly song about a girl'. And during live performances Chris frequently replaces 'Honey' with 'Jonny'. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Name: Warning Sign
Notes: Track 8 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. Written during a painful time during Chris' life, making him not want it on the album. It supposely took Jonny over a year to record his part on the song. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head

Notes: Track 9 of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. Written after the band had decided they wanted a song in 3/4 timing. It was considered the likeliest B-Side by the band themselves. The song has only ever been played live twice, once in 2014. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Era: A Rush of Blood to the Head

Notes: Track 10 and the title track of A Rush Of Blood To The Head. Written as a tribute to Bob Dylan, Johnny Cash, & Hank Williams. It also took the longest time to write out of the rest of the tracks, despite being called 'the simplest song on the album'. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Square One
Notes: Track 1 of X&Y. The song was started by a guitar riff from Jonny, who later jammed on the song with Will after showing him the riff. The song was finished above their studio and was produced by Ken Nelson. It also features Matt McGinn on guitar. Robert Smith (The Cure) is credited as a programmer. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: What If
Notes: Track 2 of X&Y. Originally written during the AROBTTH tour, the band recorded several versions across many different studios before the final stuck. Produced by Ken Nelson. It was later released as a promo single in 2006.

Name: White Shadows
Notes: Track 3 of X&Y. Considered to be the lead single before almost being entirely scrapped, though it was saved by Guy. Features Brian Eno playing the synth and the song was produced by Ken Nelson. Inspired by Tears for Fears.

Name: Fix You
Notes: Track 4 of X&Y and its second single. Fix You is considered the 'anchor' of X&Y and the rest of the album was built around it. The song was also partially written for Gwyneth Paltrow's father who had recently died. There were a few different recordings but the original version (recorded in Chicago) won. Inspired by The Pixies and Jimmy Cliff. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Talk
Notes: Track 5 of X&Y and its third single. Several members of the band (particularly Guy) dislike this song. It has the most recordings out of all X&Y tracks and was almost scrapped from the album. It samples Kraftwerk's Computer Love and is produced by Danton Supple. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Notes: Track 6 and the title tack of X&Y. It was the first song to be written for the album, dating back to the AROBTTH tour. It took a long time for the band to get the verse right. Heavily inspired by The Beatles. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Speed of Sound
Notes: Track 7 and the lead single of X&Y. Written during Summer 2004 in Chris Martin's house. Inspired by Kate Bush's Running Up That Hill & Nick Cave. Chris is unhappy with how the song out, and claims they messed the recording up. Produced by Danton Supple. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: A Message
Notes: Track 8 of X&Y. The final song written for X&Y - it was written in the middle of the night, by Chris, fully naked, playing the same guitar he recorded Square One with. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Low
Notes: Track 9 of X&Y. It was first written in Zurich (which was the song's title at the time) and supposedly reignited the band's passion for playing together. Wine glasses were used as percussion at the request of Brian Eno, who also played synths on the song. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: The Hardest Part
Notes: Track 10 of X&Y and its fourth single. Heavily inspired by R.E.M.'s Losing My Religion, which nearly caused the song to be scrapped due to the similarities between the 2. Produced by Danton Supple. Guy Berryman perfoms backing vocals.

Name: Swallowed in the Sea
Notes: Track 11 of X&Y. Like Fix You, the song was an anchor of the album *and* the band. It was inspired partly by The Pogues' Fairytale Of New York. It is one of Will's favourites from the album. It was written in 4 minutes and produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Twisted Logic
Notes: Track 12 of X&Y, and it's official final track. Written in Summer 2004 and was inspired by Muse and Samuel Barber. X&Y's world tour 'Twisted Logic' is named after the song despite never being played live. It is produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Til Kingdom Come
Notes: Track 13 of X&Y, though it is technically a hidden track. The song was recorded in 1 take by all 4 members and was originally meant to feature Johnny Cash, but he passed away before he could record for it. The song isn't on some first edition CD prints of the album. Produced by Ken Nelson.

Name: Life in Technicolor
Notes: Track 1 of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. The song is entirely instrumental apart from some 'ohhs' - it originally had lyrics but they were cut due to being 'too obvious of a single'. It samples Jon Hopkins' Light Through The Veins. Produced by Hopkins, Brian Eno, & Markus Dravs. Features strings from Davide Rossi. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals. The song transitions into Cemeteries of London.

Name: Cemeteries of London
Notes: Track 2 on Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. Considered to be Coldplays take a on "The Smiths"-esque song. This track originally contained a verse about drowning witches that was cut for being "too morbid and horrifying". Vocals were recorded in a Barcelona Church. A music video was also created and unfortunately scrapped - there is however an image online. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: Lost!
Notes: Track 3 and the third single of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. It was supposedly written during a soundcheck in 2003 where the band attempted to perform 'Sing' by Blur and accidentally wrote Lost!. The song uses a stomp-stomp-clap rhythm. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Jonny Buckland and Guy Berryman perform backing vocals.

Track 4 of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. The band made an effort to make a song without a chorus, instead splitting it into three parts. An alternate name registered to ASCAP is 'Living In My Head'. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Features Chris Martin on electric guitar and Guy Berryman performing backing vocals. Features strings from Davide Rossi.

Name: Lovers in Japan
Notes: Track 5 of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends - being the first half of a 2 song track: Lovers in Japan / Reign of Love. The main piano riff was created by sticking tacks on piano hammers. Produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: Reign of Love
Notes: Track 5 of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends - being the second half of a 2 song track: Lovers in Japan / Reign of Love. The song was originally a 20 minute long jam, which was cut down to just 3 minutes. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs.

Name: Yes
Notes: Track 6 of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. Chris intended to sing lower in his vocal register in this song, instead of his usual falsetto and is inspired by The Velvet Underground. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Features strings from Davide Rossi. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals. The song also has a hidden track; Chinese Sleep Chant.

Name: Chinese Sleep Chant
Notes: Hidden track attached to Yes. The song was written whilst the band was under hypnosis, which is showcased by the shoegaze instrumental and hazy vocals. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals, singing alternate lyrics to Chris. Features strings from Davide Rossi.

Name: Viva la Vida
Notes: The 7th track, first title track, and second single of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. The song's title was inspired by a Frida Khalo painting of the same name, meaning: 'Long Live Life'. Chris stated that "there were about nine Viva la Vidas". Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Features strings from Davide Rossi. Features a long outro which transitions into Violet Hill. Jonny, Guy, and Eno all perform backing vocals.

Name: Violet Hill
Notes: Track 8 and the lead single of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. Features a long ambient intro produced by Davide Rossi and Jon Hopkins. The opening line and melody of Violet Hill was the first piece of music Coldplay had ever written. The name comes from a street near Abbey Road. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: Strawberry Swing
Notes: Track 9 and the final single of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. Inspired by time Chris had spent in Zimbabwe.The song was originally created in Australia and is produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs. Features Chris on electric guitar & Guy Berryman performing backing vocals. Features strings from Davide Rossi.

Name: Death and All His Friends
Notes: The 10th, final, and second title track of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. The song is a 2 part track, being made up of the piano intro 'School', and the explosive ending, 'Death And All His Friends'. The second half features vocals from what is now known as the 'Coldplay Choir', being the band and other people in the studio all singing in unison. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. The song also features a hidden track; The Escapist.

Name: The Escapist
Notes: Hidden track attached to Death and All His Friends. The song is built around Jon Hopkins' Light Through The Veins, used to loop back to the start of the album (which also starts with Hopkins' song). It is mostly instrumental but has some vocals by Chris. Produced by Brian Eno & Jon Hopkins.

Name: Life in Technicolor ii
Notes: Track 1 of the Prospekt's March EP. This version of the song is longer and features proper vocals, but is missing the Hopkins instrumental intro. It was later released as the second single of this EP. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Guy Berryman performs backing vocals.

Name: Postcards from Far Away
Notes: Track 2 of the Prospekt's March EP. It is a short, instrumental interlude played on piano. The song was originally longer with vocals but it is unknown why they were cut. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs.

Name: Glass of Water
Notes: Track 3 of the Prospekt's March EP. Written at the same time as the unreleased Famous Old Painters in late 2007. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Jonny Buckland and Guy Berryman perform backing vocals.

Name: Rainy Day

Name: Prospekt's March

The song originally featured drums and heavy guitar riffs, but was later scrapped. Produced by Jon Hopkins, Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Jonny Buckland and Guy Berryman perform backing vocals.

Name: Poppyfields

Name: Mylo Xyloto
Notes: The first and title track of Mylo Xyloto. Instrumental interlude used to transition into Hurts Like Heaven. The song is named after the main character of the album's storyline. Produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs.

Name: Hurts Like Heaven
Notes: Track 2 and the final single of Mylo Xyloto. The song was written around 2 riffs that Jonny had written. Jon Hopkins plays keyboards & Davide Rossi performs strings. Produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs. Jonny and Guy perform backing vocals.

Name: Paradise
Notes: Track 3 and the second single of Mylo Xyloto. Originally written in 2010 as a gift to the winner of the X Factor, but kept by the band by Will as he thought it was too good to give away. After writing the song, the band realised they couldn't perfom it in an acoustic style, therefore scrapping The Wedding Album. Produced by Markus Dravs & Brian Eno. Davide Rossi performs strings. Jonny and Guy perform backing vocals. Jon Hopkins is credited on the song too.

Name: Charlie Brown
Notes: Track 4 and the third single of Mylo Xyloto. Originally written in 2009 after a Bruce Springsteen concert, the song was planned for The Wedding Album and was to be played on accordion. Similarly to Paradise, this changed when they released it didn't sound as good as it could be. Rossi performs strings, Hopkins plays keyboards. Produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs. Guy and J perform backing vocals.

Name: Us Against the World
Notes: Track 5 of Mylo Xyloto. Originally written in around 2009, the song was to be part of The Wedding Album before it was scrapped. Chris stated it was sort of a 'meeting' point of the 2 main characters in the story. It was intitally released as a demo but was later finished under the name 'Silver Bird' featuring an extended bridge. Produced by Brian Eno and Markus Dravs.

Name: M.M.I.X.
Notes: Track 6 of Mylo Xyloto. Instrumental interlude used to transition into Every Teardrop is a Waterfall. The song's name comes from the phrase 'Matt McGinn Is Awesome' (Jonny's guitar tech). Produced by Eno & Dravs.

Name: Every Teardop Is a Waterfall
Notes: Track 7 and the lead single of Mylo Xyloto. The song sampled 'I Go To Rio' by Peter Allen - the chords of this song were used in a 2010 film called 'Biutiful' which Chris watched. It inspired him to write the song. Davide Rossi on strings. Produced by Eno & Dravs. Jon Hopkins is also credited on the song.

Name: Major Minus
Notes: Track 8 of Mylo Xyloto. It was originally released as a B-Side to Every Teardrop Is a Waterfall on its EP. The song stemmed from another song called The Man Who Swears He's God, from the Viva La Vida sessions. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs.

Name: U.F.O.
Notes: Track 9 of Mylo Xyloto. It was potentially written for The Wedding Album in 2009, though this is unconfirmed. It was however originally combined with the title track under the name 'Great Expectations'. Produced by Eno & Dravs. It was later released as a promo single with Up With The Birds. The end of the song features an interlude into Princess of China.

Name:
Princess of China
(feat. Rihanna)
Notes: Track 10 and the fourth single of Mylo Xyloto. It was originally written for Rihanna a few years earlier, but they decided to keep it instead with Rihanna singing duet. The song samples both Takk... by Sigur Ros & Ra Ngõ Tụng Kinh by Hà Trần. Davide Rossi perfoms strings. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. Jonny, Guy, Tim Wheeler & Rik Simpson all perform backing vocals.

Name: Up in Flames
Notes: Track 11 of Mylo Xyloto. It was the last song to be made for the album, potentially replacing the famous Car Kids. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs. It was later released as a promo single.

Name: A Hopeful Transmission
Notes: Track 12 of Mylo Xyloto. Instrumental interlude used to transition into Don't Let It Break Your Heart. It was originally a full song with lyrics, but that version was scrapped. Produced by Brian Eno & Markus Dravs.

Name: A Head Full of Dreams

Miracles
(from the Unbroken Soundtrack)
Notes: Written for Angelina Jolie’s movie Unbroken. Originallly called Out Of This World. The song was written about the main character of the film, set during World War ii. Produced by Stargate.

Name: A Head Full of Dreams
Notes:
OG Filename: 01 A Head Full Of Dreams FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
The first and title track of A Head Full of Dreams. The song was originally called Family Tree, and then changed to just Head Full Of Dreams. This version of the song was almost completely different but kept some aspects. The lyric 'conference of birds' comes from a 12th century poem of the same name. Several people including the band's children and also Beyonce's daughter created the chant on the bridge. Produced by Stargate, who also co-wrote the song.

Name: Birds
Notes:
OG Filename: 02 Birds FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 2 of A Head Full of Dreams. The acoustic guitar in the song comes from Chris badly improvising and noodling. Davide Rossi adds strings. Produced by Stargate.

Name:
Hymn for the Weekend
(feat. Beyoncé)
Notes:
OG Filename: 03 Hymn For The Weekend FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 3 and the second single of A Head Full of Dreams. Originally came from the lyric 'Drinks on Me' which was changed as the band didn't think it was good. Beyoncé conbtributes vocals throughout, including a long intro where mutlple of her vocal takes are compiled together. Produced by Stargate. Avicii is also credited on the song.

Name: Everglow
Notes:
OG Filename: 04 Everglow FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 4 of A Head Full of Dreams. Gwyneth Paltrow came up with some of the lyrics, leading to her singing backing vocals on those. Due to some technical issues during a show, Chris played Everglow acoustically on piano. This version would later be released the album's final single. Produced by Stargate.

Name: Adventure of a Lifetime
Notes:
OG Filename: 05 Adventure Of A Lifetime FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 5 and the lead single of A Head Full of Dreams. The song stemmed from a demo called Legends, which was based off of a guitar riff Jonny made at Chris' request. Produced by Stargate, who also co-wrote the song. Merry Clayton performs backing vocals.

Name:
Fun
(feat. Tove Lo)
Notes:
OG Filename: 06 Fun FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 6 of A Head Full of Dreams. Chris reached out to Tove Lo to sing backing vocals on the song, which she then recorded in LA. The main riff in the song is taken from a 2011 demo called Tomorrow. Produced by Stargate. Despite Tove Lo opening for the band during the AHFOD tour, the song has never been played live.

Name:
Kaleidoscope
(feat. Coleman Barks & Barack Obama)
Notes:
OG Filename: 07 Kaleidoscope FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 7 of A Head Full of Dreams. The first half of the song features Coleman Barks reading Rumi's 'The Guesthouse' poem, while Khatia Buniatishvili plays piano. The second half features samples Barack Obama performing Amazing Grace a the funeral of Reverend Clementa C. Pinckney. Produced by Stargate.

Name: Army of One
Notes:
OG Filename: 08 Army Of One FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 8 of A Head Full of Dreams. Produced by Stargate. Daniel Green is credited for keyboards along with Chris. Includes a hidden track; X Marks The Spot.

Name: X Marks The Spot
Notes:
OG Filename: 08 Army Of One FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Hidden track after Army of One. Rough song with Chris singing vocals over a trap beat. Produced by Stargate.

Name: Amazing Day
Notes:
OG Filename: 09 Amazing Day FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 9 of A Head Full of Dreams. It was the first song from the album to be debuted live, on September 26th, 2015 at the Global Citizen Festival. Produced by Stargate. Davide Rossi adds strings.

Name: Colour Spectrum
Notes:
OG Filename: 10 Colour Spectrum FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
Track 10 of A Head Full of Dreams. Instrumental interlude featuring samples of A Head Full Of Dreams, Kaleidoscope, Hymn For The Weekend and Adventure Of A Lifetime. Produced and co-written by Stargate. Transitions into Up&Up.

Name: Up&Up
Notes:
OG Filename: 11 Up And Up FNL MSTR REF 10.5.15
The 11th, final track and third single of A Head Full of Dreams. A guitar riff for the song was written and performed by Noel Gallagher. Moses Martin also plays tambourine. Produced by Stargate, who also co-wrote the song. Several people sung vocals throughout the song, including: 

Chris Martin, Will Champion, Apple Martin, Annabelle Wallis, Merry Clayton, Beyoncé, Alison Martin, Aubrey Costall, Ava Champion, Blue Ivy Carter, Brian Eno, Violet Buckland, Harvey Costall, Elise Eriksen, Daniel Grollo, Hege Fossum Eriksen, Idil Hermansen, Isak Hermansen, Jacob Green, James Duncan, Jonah Buckland, Juno Champion, Kat Grollo, Marianna Champion, Mathilda Grollo, Max Harvey, Nico Berryman, Rafi Harvey, Rex Champion, Selma Eriksen & Sophia Green.

The song uses elements from a 2017 unreleased song called Life Is Beautiful, with 2020 demos including a bridge featuring the song's melody. Co-written by Max Martin, Oscar Hotler, Jon Hopkins, Stephen Fry, Daniel Green & Federico Vindver. Produced by Martin & Holter. Moses Martin sings Backing Vocals alongside The Love Choir. It was later released as a promo single.

Notes:
Track 7 of Music of the Spheres. Originally written at the end of 2005 under the name 'The Man Who Swears He's God' before being pulled out in around 2020 being retitled to Work. The song is about LGBT Pride and is likely about the evil 'Major Minus' from the MX era. Samples Sam Sparro's Black and Gold as well as an interlude made by Derek Dixie for Beyonce. Produced and co-wrtten by Max Martin & Oscar Hotler. Later released as a promo single. 

The song represents 'Ultra' in The Spheres Solar System.

Notes:
Track 8 and the final single of Music of the Spheres. Originally written during the Everyday Life era. The song features 'The Weirdos', a new concept featuring puppets as aliens. The leader singer is Angel Moon, AKA Angelina, who previously was on Cry Cry Cry. Davide Rossi adds strings. Produced and Co-Written by MXM & Holter.

The song represents 'Floris' in The Spheres Solar System.

Originally the song was planned to be fully English lyrics, until somebody had suggested to Chris that the band should work with BTS, leading to a verse & bridge being written/sung in Korean. The title for the song was inspired by a text message Chris had gotten. Produced and Co-Written by MXM & Holter.

It was originally shorter (around 5 mins) at Max Martin's request but the band fought to make it longer. The long ambient intro comes from a 2017 jam of Weirdo. Produced and co-written by MXM & Holter. Davide Rossi performs strings & Paris Strother played synth.

The song represents 'Coloratura' in The Spheres Solar System, which is considered the afterlife.

(with Jon Hopkins)
Notes: The first and title track of Moon Music. The first half is a pitched down sample of Jon Hopkins' Forever Held, which was unreleased at the time. The second half is an instrumental piano piece named Elodie with vocals added on. Produced by Max Martin, co-written with Jon Hopkins.

Name: feelslikeimfallinginlove
Notes: Track 2 and the lead single of Moon Music. Originally stemmed from 2 songs called My Heart and FRNDZ, the latter of which turned into Man In The Moon. The song's title is all one word due to everything feeling 'whole' when you have love. Like My Heart, the song samples Funeral Singers by Sylvan Esso. Produced by MXM. Co-written with Apple Martin, Jon Hopkins, MXM & Tim Rutili.

Name:
WE PRAY
(feat. Little Simz, Burna Boy, Elyanna, TINI & The Love Choir)
Notes: Track 3 and the second single of Moon Music. The song has four main versions, three with each artist having their own verses minus Burna Boy, and another with an instrumental second verse. It was made with the intention of having a song with voices from all around the world. Produced by MXM and ILYA. Co-Written with MXM, ILYA, Jay-Z & Davide Rossi, who contributed strings.

Name:
JUPiTER
(feat. The Love Choir)
Notes: Track 4 of Moon Music. The song went through many different genres and styles, almost leading to it being scrapped, before settling with an acoustic rendition. It is heavily inspired by the LGBT community, with the chorus leading with 'I Love Who I Love'. An extended outro features 'Jupiter Outro' - a mini-track featuring elements of Jupiter's demos, leading into a snippet of 2 Aliens, a scrapped song. Produced by MXM and ILYA. Co-Written with Orlando Flemming, MXM, ILYA & Davide Rossi. Jacob Collier, Victoria Canal, H.E.R. and Moses Martin all contribute backing vocals.

Name:
GOOD FEELiNGS
(feat. Ayra Starr, Nile Rodgers, The Chainsmokers, & The Love Choir)
Notes: Track 5 of Moon Music. The song originated when The Chainsmokers came to the band with a loop they didn't want to use, which turned into a rough e-piano led demo. The band would then invite Nile Rodgers to jam on the studio, turning the song into a funk-pop stadium banger. Angel Moon makes her grand return for this song, singing backup vocals on the choruses. During early 2025, Elyanna sung Ayra Starr's parts on the MOTSWT. Produced by MXM and The Chainsmokers.

Name:
🌈
(ALiEN HiTS / ALiEN RADiO)
Notes: Track 6 of Moon Music. The song is a 3-part suite made up of mainly of Neon Forest and Angelsong, with elements of The Karate Kid, Sunshine, Opus 5, Man In The Moon and m.u.s.i.c. being spliced throughout. It is about different styles of music throughout the galaxy. Its name originally comes from 2009, likely meant to be included on Mylo Xyloto. Produced by MXM and Jon Hopkins. Co-Written with Kaori Muraji, Jon Hopkins, Max Martin, Maya Angelou (who's speech was sampled during Angelsong) & Devin Powers.

Name:
iAAM
(i AM A MOUNTAiN)
Notes: Track 7 of Moon Music. Originally written in 2019, Chris struggled to write the verses. Eventually they would be written using lyrics from an early version of JUPiTER. During early 2024 the song was performed at a soundcheck, sparking interest in what it could be. Included on FC25's soundtrack, allowing fans to hear the song early. Produced and co-written by MXM.

Name:
AETERNA
(feat. The Love Choir)
Notes: Track 8 of Moon Music. An snippet of an early demo was occasionally played during The Lightclub section of the MOTSWT. Seen in Chris' Moon Music Notebook, the song is confirmed to have a Part 2, which is also a prelude. Produced by MXM. Co-Written with MXM & Louis Cole (whose song was sampled). We Are KING, Jacob Collier, Jon Hopkins & Victoria Canal contribute backing vocals.

Name: feelslikeimfallinginlove Pt. 2
Notes: Hidden track on AETERNA. Features the phrase 'I Love You' being repeated in an african language by Laura Mvula.

Name: ALL MY LOVE
Notes: Track 9 and the third single of Moon Music. Confirmed to be Coldplay's final 'proper' single. The whole album was supposedly built around the song, going back to the style of the band's older music. During a show in early 2024, a comedian tried to climb onto the stage during Biutyful, the show's last song. Due to this Chris decided to debut the song to the world 4 months earlier than intended. Produced by MXM & ILYA. H.E.R. contributes backing vocals.

Name:
ONE WORLD
(feat. The Love Choir, Brian Eno, and many more)
Notes: The 10th and final track of Moon Music. The song starts off with Chris repeating the phrase 'only one world' 6 times before over 100,000 voices hum 'one'. This was requested by the band in late 2023, where fans were invited to record vocals for the song. The song then breaks out into full band, ending with 'in the end it's just love'. Produced by MXM. Co-Written with MXM & Brian Eno. Around 120,000 unique vocals are featured.
